content_html:
A shower curtain collects soap residue, minerals, and biofilm because it stays damp after each use. The right method depends on the material and whether the buildup is on the decorative curtain, the inner liner, or both.

Separate the curtain and liner before choosing a method

Fabric, vinyl, other plastic liners, and specialty coatings do not all tolerate the same cleaning. Check the care label on each piece and treat the curtain and liner according to their own materials.

Remove soap residue before treating dark spots

Soap film can hide the surface and trap soil. Use a compatible detergent, rinse thoroughly, and then reassess any remaining dark spots that may need more targeted treatment.

Machine-wash only when the care label allows it

Some fabric curtains tolerate a gentle cycle, while certain plastic liners can deform with agitation or heat. If machine washing is allowed, use the specified temperature and never mix incompatible cleaning products.

Leave it spread out to dry between showers

A bunched curtain takes much longer to dry. Spread it after showering, improve bathroom ventilation, and clean it before buildup becomes a thick layer that is difficult to remove.
